## JustGo_mobile: 5-minute windows where avg view duration exceeded 30 s
Built on the same `makeTimeseries { avg_ms = avg(toDouble(duration)) }, by: { os.name }` as the JustGo_mobile chart, at a **5-minute interval**. The first tile lists every window where an OS's average went over **30 s**, newest first (`Time start`, `avg_ms` in ms, `User events`, `OS`). The second tile shows the same windows **one row each**, with the **3 slowest services tagged `JustGo`** side by side: for each of #1–#3 a `service`, `response (ms)` and `requests` column for those 5 minutes. Default timeframe: last 24 hours.

- `User events` is the number of JustGo_mobile view events with a `duration` in that OS's window, i.e. the events the `avg_ms` was calculated from.
- `duration` is stored in nanoseconds, so the threshold is `30000000000` (30 s) and `avg_ms` is divided by 1,000,000 for display.
- Service response time (`dt.service.request.response_time`, microseconds) is shown in ms; request count is `dt.service.request.count` summed over the window.
- Beyond a few days Dynatrace widens the 5-minute interval (both tiles widen together), so each row then covers a longer window.

sections.title: JustGo_mobile 5-minute windows with avg view duration > 30 s

input.value:
fetch user.events
| filter characteristics.has_view_summary == true
| filter frontend.name == "JustGo_mobile"
| makeTimeseries { avg_ms = avg(toDouble(duration)), user_events = countIf(isNotNull(duration)) }, by: { os.name }, interval: 5m
// one row per OS per 5-minute window
| fieldsAdd pts = iCollectArray(record(time_start = timeframe[start] + interval * iIndex(), v = avg_ms[], n = user_events[]))
| expand pts
// duration is in nanoseconds: 30 s = 30,000,000,000 ns
| filter pts[v] > 30000000000
| fields `Time start` = pts[time_start], avg_ms = round(pts[v] / 1000000, decimals: 0), `User events` = pts[n], OS = os.name
| sort `Time start` desc

sections.title: Top 3 slowest JustGo services in each > 30 s window

input.value:
fetch user.events
| filter characteristics.has_view_summary == true
| filter frontend.name == "JustGo_mobile"
| makeTimeseries { avg_ms = avg(toDouble(duration)), user_events = countIf(isNotNull(duration)) }, by: { os.name }, interval: 5m
// one row per OS per 5-minute window; keep windows over 30 s (duration is in ns)
| fieldsAdd pts = iCollectArray(record(time_start = timeframe[start] + interval * iIndex(), v = avg_ms[], n = user_events[]))
| expand pts
| filter pts[v] > 30000000000
| fields time_start = pts[time_start], avg_ms = pts[v] / 1000000, user_events = pts[n], os.name
// response time and request count of every JustGo-tagged service, per 5-minute window
| join [
    timeseries { rt = avg(dt.service.request.response_time), req = sum(dt.service.request.count) },
      by: { dt.entity.service },
      filter: { in(dt.entity.service, classicEntitySelector("type(SERVICE),tag(JustGo)")) },
      interval: 5m
    | fieldsAdd service = entityName(dt.entity.service)
    | fieldsAdd pts = iCollectArray(record(ts = timeframe[start] + interval * iIndex(), rt_ms = rt[] / 1000, req = req[]))
    | expand pts
    | fields ts = pts[ts], rt_ms = pts[rt_ms], req = pts[req], service
    | filter isNotNull(rt_ms)
  ], kind: leftOuter, on: { left[time_start] == right[ts] }, fields: { service, rt_ms, req }
// 3 slowest services per breach window
| summarize { services = collectArray(record(rt_ms, service, req)) }, by: { time_start, os.name, avg_ms, user_events }
| fieldsAdd top3 = arraySlice(arraySort(services, direction: "descending"), from: 0, to: 3)
// one row per breach window: the 3 slowest services side by side, each with its own response time and request count
| fields `Time start` = time_start, `Time end` = time_start + 5m, OS = os.name,
    avg_ms = round(avg_ms, decimals: 0), `User events` = user_events,
    `#1 service` = top3[0][service], `#1 response (ms)` = round(top3[0][rt_ms], decimals: 1), `#1 requests` = toLong(top3[0][req]),
    `#2 service` = top3[1][service], `#2 response (ms)` = round(top3[1][rt_ms], decimals: 1), `#2 requests` = toLong(top3[1][req]),
    `#3 service` = top3[2][service], `#3 response (ms)` = round(top3[2][rt_ms], decimals: 1), `#3 requests` = toLong(top3[2][req])
| sort `Time start` desc, avg_ms desc

## JustGo_mobile failures: client connectivity vs application failure
The tile below classifies every 5-minute window (per OS) that has failed requests or crashes. It labels a window as *likely* client connectivity or as an application failure. **It does not diagnose ISPs.** The thresholds are a **proposal to agree on**.

**Signals used (RUM on Grail):** `characteristics.has_failed_request`, `http.response.status_code` (empty = no server response), `network.connection.type` / `network.carrier.name`, iOS `error.reason` + `error.code` (NSURLErrorDomain), Android `exception.type` / `exception.message` (`java.net.*`), `characteristics.has_crash`, and distinct devices (`dt.rum.instance.id`). These are correlated with backend health of `JustGo`-tagged services in the same window: failure rate and average response time.

**Per-request signals**
- *Network error* (connectivity signal): connection type offline/none; iOS codes -1009 not connected, -1005 connection lost, -1004 cannot connect, -1003 host not found, -1020 data not allowed, -1018 roaming off, -1006 DNS; Android UnknownHost / Connect / NoRouteToHost, "network is unreachable", "connection reset".
- *Timeout*: iOS -1001, SocketTimeoutException, "timed out". Counts as connectivity **only if the backend average response time is under 5 s**.
- *Cancelled* (iOS -999, "cancel"): **excluded**. These are user navigation or the app being backgrounded, not failures.
- *HTTP 5xx / 4xx*: the server answered, so these are **never connectivity**.

**Window classification (first match wins)**
1. Fewer than 5 failures and crashes → *Low volume, not classified*.
2. 5xx ≥ 50% of failures **or** backend failure rate ≥ 5% → *Confirmed application failure*.
3. Crashes ≥ failed requests → *Confirmed application failure (crash)*.
4. 4xx ≥ 50% of failures → *Application/client request error (4xx)*.
5. Network errors + qualifying timeouts ≥ 50% of failures, **and** backend healthy (< 1% failures, < 5 s), **and** < 20% of active devices affected → *Likely client connectivity*.
6. Network-type or no-response failures ≥ 50% but systemic (≥ 20% of devices) or backend degraded → *Possible infrastructure or edge issue, review*. Examples: DNS, CDN, load balancer, or an outage on a shared network path.
7. Anything else → *Unclassified, review*.

**False-positive handling**
- Timeouts during slow backend windows are treated as application-side, not as connectivity.
- Many devices failing at once is treated as systemic, never as "the users' connection".
- Cancelled requests are excluded. Low-volume windows are not labelled.
- Windows with no backend data say "backend no data". Connectivity is then only *likely*, never confirmed.
- `Carriers` and `Connection types` give context only. One carrier dominating is still *likely client connectivity*, not an ISP finding.

**Recommended next step:** if the app can report a reliable connectivity state, send it as a custom event or event property, for example `connectivity.state = offline|online` on change. Use it as the strongest connectivity signal in rule 5. Some fields above, such as `error.code` and `exception.*` on request events, may not be populated by every agent version. Check them on the JustGo tenant before relying on the counts.

sections.title: JustGo_mobile failures: likely client connectivity vs application failure

input.value:
fetch user.events
| filter frontend.name == "JustGo_mobile"
| filter characteristics.has_request == true or characteristics.has_crash == true
| fieldsAdd has_request = coalesce(characteristics.has_request, false),
    has_failed = coalesce(characteristics.has_failed_request, false),
    has_crash = coalesce(characteristics.has_crash, false)
// ---- 1. per request: what kind of failure is it? ----
| fieldsAdd status = toLong(http.response.status_code),
    err_txt = lower(concat(coalesce(exception.type, ""), " ", coalesce(exception.message, ""), " ", coalesce(error.reason, ""))),
    ios_code = coalesce(toLong(error.code), 0)
| fieldsAdd is_cancelled = has_failed and (ios_code == -999 or contains(err_txt, "cancel"))
| fieldsAdd is_timeout = has_failed and not is_cancelled and (ios_code == -1001 or contains(err_txt, "timeout") or contains(err_txt, "timed out"))
| fieldsAdd is_conn = has_failed and not is_cancelled and not is_timeout and (
      coalesce(in(lower(network.connection.type), array("offline", "none", "no_network")), false)
      or in(ios_code, array(-1009, -1005, -1004, -1003, -1020, -1018, -1006))
      or contains(err_txt, "no_network") or contains(err_txt, "unknownhost") or contains(err_txt, "unable to resolve host")
      or contains(err_txt, "connectexception") or contains(err_txt, "failed to connect") or contains(err_txt, "noroutetohost")
      or contains(err_txt, "network is unreachable") or contains(err_txt, "connection reset") or contains(err_txt, "connection abort")
      or contains(err_txt, "not connected to the internet") or contains(err_txt, "network connection was lost"))
| fieldsAdd no_response = has_failed and not is_cancelled and (isNull(status) or coalesce(status, 0) == 0)
// ---- 2. per 5-minute window and OS ----
| summarize {
    requests = countIf(has_request),
    failed = countIf(has_failed and not is_cancelled),
    cancelled = countIf(is_cancelled),
    conn = countIf(is_conn),
    timeouts = countIf(is_timeout),
    no_resp_other = countIf(no_response and not is_conn and not is_timeout),
    http5xx = countIf(has_failed and coalesce(status, 0) >= 500),
    http4xx = countIf(has_failed and coalesce(status, 0) >= 400 and coalesce(status, 0) < 500),
    crashes = countIf(has_crash),
    active_devices = countDistinctExact(dt.rum.instance.id),
    failed_devices = countDistinctExact(if(has_failed and not is_cancelled, dt.rum.instance.id)),
    conn_devices = countDistinctExact(if(is_conn or is_timeout, dt.rum.instance.id)),
    carriers = countDistinctExact(if(is_conn or is_timeout, network.carrier.name)),
    conn_types = arrayRemoveNulls(collectDistinct(if(is_conn or is_timeout, network.connection.type)))
  }, by: { time_start = bin(timestamp, 5m), os.name }
| filter failed > 0 or crashes > 0
// ---- 3. backend health of JustGo-tagged services in the same 5 minutes ----
| join [
    timeseries { req = sum(dt.service.request.count), fail = sum(dt.service.request.failure_count), rt = avg(dt.service.request.response_time) },
      filter: { in(dt.entity.service, classicEntitySelector("type(SERVICE),tag(JustGo)")) }, interval: 5m
    | fieldsAdd pts = iCollectArray(record(ts = timeframe[start] + interval * iIndex(), req = req[], fail = fail[], rt = rt[]))
    | expand pts
    | fields ts = pts[ts], be_req = pts[req], be_fail_pct = 100.0 * pts[fail] / pts[req], be_rt_ms = pts[rt] / 1000
  ], kind: leftOuter, on: { left[time_start] == right[ts] }, fields: { be_req, be_fail_pct, be_rt_ms }
// ---- 4. classification (thresholds are the rules to agree) ----
| fieldsAdd conn_like = conn + if(coalesce(be_rt_ms, 0) < 5000, timeouts, else: 0),
    devices_pct = 100.0 * failed_devices / active_devices
| fieldsAdd backend_bad = coalesce(be_fail_pct, 0) >= 5, backend_warn = coalesce(be_fail_pct, 0) >= 1 or coalesce(be_rt_ms, 0) >= 5000
| fieldsAdd Classification = if(failed + crashes < 5, "Low volume - not classified",
    else: if(http5xx >= 0.5 * failed or backend_bad, "Confirmed application failure",
    else: if(crashes > 0 and crashes >= failed, "Confirmed application failure (crash)",
    else: if(http4xx >= 0.5 * failed, "Application/client request error (4xx)",
    else: if(conn_like >= 0.5 * failed and not backend_warn and devices_pct < 20, "Likely client connectivity",
    else: if(conn_like + no_resp_other >= 0.5 * failed, "Possible infrastructure or edge issue - review",
    else: "Unclassified - review"))))))
| fieldsAdd Reason = concat(
    toString(conn), " network, ", toString(timeouts), " timeout, ", toString(http5xx), " 5xx, ", toString(http4xx), " 4xx of ", toString(failed), " failed",
    "; ", toString(round(devices_pct, decimals: 0)), "% of devices hit",
    "; backend ", if(isNull(be_fail_pct), "no data", else: concat(toString(round(be_fail_pct, decimals: 1)), "% failed, ", toString(round(be_rt_ms, decimals: 0)), " ms")))
| fields `Time start` = time_start, OS = os.name, Classification, Reason,
    `Failed requests` = failed, `Network errors` = conn, Timeouts = timeouts, `No response (other)` = no_resp_other,
    `HTTP 5xx` = http5xx, `HTTP 4xx` = http4xx, Crashes = crashes,
    `Devices affected` = failed_devices, `% devices affected` = round(devices_pct, decimals: 1), `Carriers (network failures)` = carriers,
    `Connection types` = conn_types, `Backend failure %` = round(be_fail_pct, decimals: 2), `Backend avg response (ms)` = round(be_rt_ms, decimals: 0),
    `Cancelled (excluded)` = cancelled
| sort `Time start` desc

## Preview with mock data
The tile below runs **the same query on generated data**, so you can see the table with breaches. It makes up JustGo_mobile view events for Android, iOS and iPadOS over the last hour (3 per minute). Android goes over 30 s for two minutes and iOS for one; iPadOS never does. Times move with the current time. Nothing here reads real data.
